entities.summary: Howard Winchel Koch was an American film producer and director. He served as president of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and as head of film production at Paramount Pictures, and directed and produced numerous films, including The Manchurian Candidate (1962), The Odd Couple (1968), Airplane! (1980) and its 1982 sequel, and Ghost (1990). At the 62nd Academy Awards, he was honored the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award for his "outstanding contributions to humanitarian causes". He also received four Primetime Emmy Award nominations, three of which were for producing Academy Awards ceremonies.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As president of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and head of film production at Paramount Pictures, Koch's influence on American popular culture was significant, with films like The Manchurian Candidate and Airplane! contributing to the development of comedy and thriller genres. His humanitarian work earned him the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award.
